headline: 50,000 young sturgeon swim free in two French rivers
summary: Researchers working for two decades to save a critically endangered fish just freed tens of thousands more in the Garonne and Dordogne. Since 2022, adults longer than two metres have been returning upstream.

headline: Colorado's Giant Wildlife Bridge Cuts Crashes With Animals by 91%
summary: Ten months after a huge overpass opened above Interstate 25 near Larkspur, Colorado, data shows far fewer vehicle strikes on wildlife. The crossing spans six lanes and serves species such as elk and moose.

headline: Ghana's malaria deaths drop 98% in little over a decade
summary: Annual deaths nationwide went from 3,300 in 2011 to 52 last year. A hospital in Cape Coast, led on infectious disease by Elisabeth Tabitha Abbew, reports no malaria deaths for two years.

headline: Hainan gibbons, once nearly gone, grow to 44 animals on their island home
summary: After falling to roughly seven animals by the 1980s, the Hainan gibbon population now stands at 44, spread across seven families. Rangers follow their morning calls, and 300,000 food trees have been planted for them.

headline: Germany's coal and gas power output has dropped by almost half since 2018
summary: Comparing the first six months of 2018 and 2026, the federal statistics office found fossil-fuel electricity fell from 174.6 to 94.2 terawatt-hours, down 46%. Renewables now provide close to 60% of the country's power.

headline: Kosovo's Minefields Are Now Fully Cleared, a Job Nearly Three Decades Long
summary: The demining charity HALO Trust has wrapped up its work in Kosovo. Thousands of local people on its staff over the decades helped make the land safe, and the organization says its mission was built to end.

headline: World life expectancy nearly recovers from its pandemic dip
summary: WHO estimates put the worldwide average at 73.3 for 2023, just a tenth of a year shy of 2019's 73.4. In low-income countries, infectious diseases now make up under half of deaths, a first.

headline: Fewer U.S. high schoolers report deep sadness and suicidal thoughts
summary: CDC figures show 33% of high schoolers felt persistently sad in 2025, down from 42% four years earlier. Those who seriously considered suicide dropped to 14%, compared with 22% in 2021.

headline: South Korea now recycles nearly all its food scraps, once buried
summary: In 1997, about 95% of the country's food waste was dumped in the ground; now roughly 95% gets recycled. Weighed bins, sorted pickup and a 2005 dumping prohibition helped, with Seoul's daily waste falling almost 25%.

headline: Ocean protection passes 10% worldwide for the first time
summary: Roughly 5 million km² of sea, an area bigger than the EU, gained protection in a recent two-year span. With over 100 countries now backing the High Seas Treaty, more gains may follow.

headline: Melting Norwegian Ice Gives Up 48 Ancient Arrow Parts in Two-Decade Search
summary: Researchers in southern Norway have spent 20 years checking glaciers for buried artifacts. Their latest haul is 48 arrowheads and shafts, made from various materials and dating to different eras.

headline: Neighbors and Officers Honored After Pulling Elderly Driver From Sinking Car
summary: During an August storm in Illinois, an older woman's car slid into a water-filled basin and began going under. Several bystanders swam out to her, and four Champaign police officers joined them.
